results.title: Anthropic Expands Claude Access for Vetted Cyber Teams as Glasswing Finds 129,000 Flaws
results.author: info@thehackernews.com (The Hacker News)
results.content:
Anthropic on Tuesday said it's expanding a program that allows vetted cybersecurity professionals to test its advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models with reduced safeguards and blocking classifiers, as the company claimed its Project Glasswing initiative uncovered at least 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities between April and July 2026.
The company said it also found an additional 5,500 verified software vulnerabilities between April and October 2026 through open-source scanning efforts.
"Of these verified vulnerabilities, more than 33,000 have so far been rated as critical- or high-severity," Anthropic said. "This is likely an undercount, as it is based on survey data from only a subset of Glasswing partners. As such, we expect the true impact to be at least five times higher."
The updated program, called the Cyber Verification Program (CVP), features three access tiers, allowing organizations and security teams to apply for one that best aligns with their work. Each tier comes with access to its models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward.
The three access levels are detailed below -
- Defense Access, which is for defensive work, such as incident response, malware reverse engineering, and vulnerability analysis and validation.
- Red Team Access, which adds authorized penetration testing and red-teaming to the defensive use cases.
- Specialized Access, which has the fewest safeguards and is reserved for a limited set of verified organizations that are authorized to test safety systems.
According to a CyScenarioBench evaluation, its safeguards blocked 46 of 50 tasks on Claude Opus 5.5 in the Defense Access tier, while the Red Team Access tier on the same model did not block any tasks, and completed 34 of 50, which is the same completion rate as when no safeguards are applied. Without CVP access, every task was blocked on the first prompt.
"These evaluations give us confidence that we can make advanced cyber capabilities safely available to a broader set of defenders, expanding the defensive efforts we began with Project Glasswing," Anthropic said.
The AI company said it's making these tools available to defenders given their dual-use nature, and to help them secure systems using the same capabilities that could be weaponized by a bad actor for malicious purposes.
In an analysis published late last month, VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity revealed that only 2 of the 300 vulnerabilities discovered by Anthropic or Project Glasswing, or 0.67%, have been exploited in the wild. Of these, 39 have been classified as critical, 141 as high, 81 as medium, and 18 as low in severity.
The two vulnerabilities that have witnessed active exploitation efforts are CVE-2026-26980, an SQL injection flaw in Ghost CMS, and CVE-2026-61500, a session forgery flaw in Rejetto HTTP File Server.
If anything, the findings suggest that while AI is lowering the barrier to vulnerability discovery, not every security flaw it uncovers is necessarily exploitable by threat actors or capable of causing significant impacts. Moreover, as demonstrated by 1Password and Veracode, AI-generated vulnerability patches can themselves introduce new security risks of their own.
"Roughly 44% of AI code generation tasks introduced a risky security vulnerability in tests," Veracode said. "The average security pass rate across models is 56% – barely changed from 55% in the first report. In other words, security performance has stayed flat while the amount of AI-generated code entering pipelines has surged."
results.summary:
Anthropic is expanding its Cyber Verification Program to provide vetted security professionals with tiered access to advanced AI models for identifying and patching critical software vulnerabilities.

### Key Points
- Anthropic’s Project Glasswing identified over 134,500 verified software vulnerabilities between April and October 2026.
- The new Cyber Verification Program offers three access tiers—Defense, Red Team, and Specialized—for testing models like Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5.
- Red Team Access allows researchers to bypass standard AI safeguards to conduct authorized penetration testing and vulnerability validation.
- Only two of the 300 vulnerabilities identified by the initiative have been exploited in the wild, according to VulnCheck research.
- Veracode reports that 44% of AI-generated code tasks introduce new security risks, highlighting ongoing challenges with automated patching.

### Why it Matters
This initiative highlights the dual-use nature of AI, which can simultaneously accelerate vulnerability discovery and introduce new security flaws into software pipelines. By providing controlled access to powerful models, Anthropic aims to empower defenders to secure systems before malicious actors can weaponize the same capabilities.

results.title: Abundantia Entertainment To Turn AI Creative Arm AiOn Into Standalone Studio: “Truly A Confluence Of Technology And Art”
results.author: Jesse Whittock
results.content:
EXCLUSIVE: This time last year, India‘s Abundantia Entertainment launched an AI production division named Abundantia AiOn. Today, we can reveal that is morphing into a fully standalone native AI studio that will seek harness in an influx of ideas from non-traditional sources.
“AiOn will develop its own stories, create its own content, produce fully generated as well as hybrid work, and manage the entire ecosystem, just as Abundantia does as a standalone studio,” Vikram Malhotra, Abundantia’s founder and CEO told Deadline during an exclusive interview.
Malhotra will remain in charge of AiOn for the time being. “For the moment, it will sit within Abundantia, but we are building it in a way that gives it its own identity and scope,” he said.
Watch on Deadline
“Workflows have become hybrid, and production and creative thinking are becoming hybrid. The capability needed to run AI at studio level will not be found solely within the conventional media and entertainment system. It is truly a confluence of technology and art.”
Malhotra said the move had been taken after receiving “three times as many pitches from people who have never written, made films or belonged to the conventional filmmaking ecosystem as I have in the past” over the last six months.
He cited the rise of directors such as Obsession‘s Curry Barker and Backrooms‘ Kane Parsons as evidence of a “democratization” of ideas that would be powered by AI studios in the future.
“AiOn defines itself as human-first and AI-empowered, and I’m seeing that happen in front of my eyes in real time,” he added.
Earlier in the year, Abundantia announced another AI studio initiative, teaming with AI video tech company InVideo to launch a film studio, which will develop a slate of five films over the next few years. That company is also teaming with Abundantia aiOn.
Malhotra, one of India’s most experienced execs and producers, launched Abundantia back in 2013 after exiting a role as COO of Viacom18 Motion Pictures and a shorter spell leading Balaji Motion Pictures. The company has since made films such as Baby, Airlift, Toilet – Ek Prem Katha, Shakuntala Devi, Sherni, and Chhorii and Chhorii 2. On the series from, it produced Prime Video’s Breathe.
This year has seen the launch of Netflix films Maa Behen and a movie and series for Prime Video, Subedaar and Daldal, respectively. The former is an action drama directed by Suresh Triveni and fronted by Anil Kapoor; and the latter an original drama series starring Bhumi Pednekar.
Maa Behen, a Hindi-language black comedy starring Madhuri Dixit and Triptii Dimri among others, was well received on Netflix. It became the #1 trending film on Netflix India in the week of its release in June and rose to #2 in global non-English films.
Subedaar, meanwhile, was notable for being Anil Kapoor’s first action movie since S. Shankar’s Nayak: A Real Hero, which was released in 2001. Malhotra addressed how he tempted the actor back to the genre (clue: It wasn’t a hard sell) and gave his assessment of the Indian production as we look ahead to 2027 and beyond.
DEADLINE: There’s a lot of interesting work going on at Abundantia right now. How has the year been so far?
Vikram Malhotra: It’s been an exciting year. We completed 13 years on the 26th of this month, and in many ways this year has been the manifestation of the 12 years that came before it – and hopefully a sign of things to come. The last nine months have been exciting for us on all fronts.
DEADLINE: What has happened that really punctuates that progress?
Malhotra: When I started building Abundantia in 2013, the fundamental gap I had identified throughout my time in the business, including at Viacom18 and Balaji, was that the supply of high-quality, progressive content for a younger, more evolved audience wasn’t meeting demand.
Abundantia was formed and built with studio economics in mind, rather than project economics. I was always focused on building an institution, rather than approaching the business on a project-by-project basis, which is often the short-sighted way demand or opportunity is evaluated in this market.
If we use 2026 as a symbol of that approach, the year has included three releases: One film on Prime Video, one series on Prime Video and one film on Netflix. We also have theatrical work lined up, more projects with those two streamers and a number of things in development. The founding philosophy remains the same: Put the customer at the heart of the business, let creativity drive the velocity of the business and continue disrupting the kinds of stories you tell.
Whittock: One of the major strategic moves you have made is into AI, including the deal with InVideo in February and your AI studio. There is a lot of discussion around AI, and companies are still working out what it means for them, but Abundantia seems to have moved beyond the theoretical stage. How would you describe the strategy?
Malhotra: AI is a strategic priority for us. It is not simply another means of reducing costs and saving time.
Throughout our journey, we have factored in technological shifts. COVID taught us how to work remotely, and we naturally began weaving that into our production workflow. When streaming arrived in India, it completely changed how hundreds of millions of Indian consumers experienced content. We were the first company from the film ecosystem to move into streaming.
I sense an even bigger opportunity with AI. Abundantia has been working on it in our own way for the past two years. As with streaming, the idea was to first understand what we were dealing with, build capability and build for the long term.
DEADLINE: Will AI end up as a positive thing for the industry, then?
Malhotra: I look at AI as an amplifier of imagination and an accelerator of growth. More importantly, I see it addressing a fundamental aspect of the content business: Risk. This business has risk built into it because risk comes from the consumer side. It is an intangible reason why people spend time and money on what we offer. Any attempt to eliminate that risk would be futile.
So we asked ourselves: Can AI help reduce the cost of going wrong? Beyond the logistical benefits – cost, time and scale – can it improve our ability to understand how and where we go wrong? If we do go wrong, can we learn quickly from those mistakes and build that learning into a replicable model? That is fundamentally how AI is built into Abundantia’s strategy.”
We have a dedicated creative division called AiOn, under which we have been doing all our AI work. I’m happy to tell you this today that in 2027 we are launching AiOn as a fully fledged, fully native AI studio. AiOn will develop its own stories, create its own content, produce fully generated as well as hybrid work, and manage the entire ecosystem, just as Abundantia does as a standalone studio.
DEADLINE: Will it remain within Abundantia?
Malhotra: For the moment, it will sit within Abundantia, but we are building it in a way that gives it its own identity and scope. Workflows have become hybrid, and production and creative thinking are becoming hybrid. The capability needed to run AI at studio level will not be found solely within the conventional media and entertainment system. It is truly a confluence of technology and art.
Technology has already disrupted the conventional media and entertainment model in two important ways. First, through funding from technology-native companies; and second, through disruption in distribution, whether via streaming or other non-conventional forms that are now mainstream. This is technology creating a new wave of creatives. AiOn is intended to harness that at a dedicated level as a native AI studio.
DEADLINE: Who will lead AiOn?
Malhotra: In the immediate term, it will remain under Abundantia’s leadership, with me leading AiOn as well. To clarify, we will continue to call it AiOn – we are not calling it AiOn Studios. I’m using that description for ease.
We will draw on Abundantia’s learning and capability across the ecosystem, from creative to screen and everything in between. We will also draw on the networks, knowledge and access we have built, while rapidly creating a similar ecosystem under AiOn. The strategy is based on the fact that we will need new skill sets. The person telling the story will still be human, but that person’s background may be very different from what we have conventionally seen.
DEADLINE: What prompted you to make this move?
Malhotra: One statistic excites me most. In the last six months, on average, I have received three times as many story pitches from people who have never written, made films or belonged to the conventional filmmaking ecosystem as I have in the past.
That is the impact of AI-driven democratization on our business. People can bounce ideas around, refine pitches, create an audiovisual package around the story they want to tell and add music. AiOn defines itself as human-first and AI-empowered, and I’m seeing that happen in front of my eyes in real time.
DEADLINE: You have spoken about two films coming out of the studio – Chiranjeevi Hanuman and Jai Santoshi Mata: Sukh Sampatti Daata. Where do those projects stand?
Malhotra: Chiranjeevi Hanuman is completing readiness. Jai Santoshi Mata is a hybrid project and is set to go on the floors early next year. The work on world-building and on every aspect of AI generation is already under way.
Beyond that, we have accelerated the slates we have been building. Our work with one of our long-standing partners, InVideo, is bearing fruit. Two films are under way, including one that is about to go on the floors, and three other scripts – with defined filmmakers, timelines and budgets – are already in development.
My understanding of using AI to create films is that the only way to do it is to get on and do it. We have accumulated significant learning through the production process of Chiranjeevi Hanuman. We are building on that as we take Jai Santoshi Mata and two other films to the floors, as we find new filmmaking voices and as we learn through consumer research.
When I say AiOn will operate like a studio, there is a reason I distinguish that from its current form as a creative division. AiOn will leverage AI across the value chain.
DEADLINE: You have mentioned the increase in pitches from non-traditional sources. In Hollywood, YouTube creators and people from the wider creator economy are moving into film and television rapidly. Are you seeing the same change in India, and are you looking in those places?
Malhotra: It is safe to say that the penetration of AI into daily life, especially among people under 35 in India, is virtually 100%. Anyone with a smartphone is experiencing AI at work. Anyone with a smart device is experiencing AI at work.
That gives me confidence and optimism. I no longer have to sell the concept. A year or 18 months ago, I was talking about upskilling writers and directors and asking how people would be able to create. People have moved so aggressively along the learning curve that those challenges are falling by the wayside.
Anyone with a story to tell now has the ability to get that story into tangible form. The democratization of distribution through YouTube, Instagram and WhatsApp means those stories can reach audiences. The gatekeepers who controlled which stories were told to the wider public are falling away.
As a studio and producer, my ability to access disruptive, non-conventional voices is greater than ever. We are constantly scouting these platforms to see whether there is a distinctive voice, a concept or a story we would otherwise not encounter. It is easier said than done, because much of the time we have to go to those creators rather than simply wait for them to come to us.
DEADLINE: So how do you harness all of this?
Malhotra: The key issue is mindset. Before you build an AI team, workflow, company or film, you need an AI mindset. I’m constantly telling my team to think about timelines, opportunity and economics as they would in technology, while retaining blue-sky thinking in the way we tell stories.
It is happening in real time. The number of pitches I receive from creators, especially those under 30, is phenomenal. Yesterday, my team and I heard a story and looked at one another, saying that it would never have occurred to someone who was native to the conventional system because it was so far outside the usual way of thinking.
There has never been a better time to be in the storytelling business. Audiences are more willing than ever to consume and accept differentiated content – look at the success of phenomena such as Obsession and Backrooms. At the other end, creators of all kinds are being empowered to tell their stories better. The challenge is to identify the right voices and build an institution around them, rather than treating them as one-off projects.
DEADLINE: Moving back to your traditional business, Abundantia has this year launched films for Prime Video and Netflix and a series for Amazon. Maa Behen performed well on Netflix and charted strongly. Are there plans to expand that universe, perhaps through a sequel or series spin-off?
Malhotra: Both films we made this year, Subedaar and Maa Behen, are built around strong central characters and large, expandable worlds. The director they have in common, Suresh Triveni, our partner and collaborator, who imagined these worlds and characters as extending beyond a single outing.
Development work is under way, given that both films landed with reasonable success. If the creative interests align, they lend themselves to franchising and future instalments without a doubt. However, a sequel should build on the original and its foundations, and it cannot depend on the original alone for its success. There has to be a solid reason for a second instalment of anything.
Whittock: There was a lot of excitement about Anil Kapoor returning to the action genre with Subedaar. Was it an easy sell, or did he need convincing?
Malhotra: Anil and I have known each other since 2011, when I was running Viacom18 and we were marketing and distributing Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol in India, which featured him. We have enjoyed each other’s company and shared sensibility ever since.
When Suresh was developing Subedaar – a unique mainstream action drama around an older hero, something Hindi cinema and much of Indian cinema is not known for – he had one actor in mind: Anil Kapoor.
At the time, Anil hadn’t led an action film for 23 years. I called him and said, ‘Anil, I’m producing this film with the wonderful director Suresh Triveni, who made Jalsa and Tumhari Sulu for us. We’re building an action film about an older ex-serviceman who takes on the system.’ Before I could ask whether he was interested, he said, ‘Done. I’m in. I’ll do the film. When do we start?’
Although it seemed like an instinctive decision, he knew the genre was right for him. He knew his audience and understood that his fans wanted to see him return in that kind of role. He also saw the creative talent involved and committed to it completely.
DEADLINE: Looking ahead to 2027 and 2028, what is the plan for Abundantia? There is a lot of money in the market, but some of it appears to be receding and the number of commissions is coming down. It feels like a difficult place to work if you don’t know what you’re doing – commissions and greenlights are no longer being handed out simply to meet the demand created by the streaming boom. How do you read the market?
Malhotra: That’s a fantastic assessment. India is an unforgiving market because it is made up of extremely value-conscious consumers. The Indian content consumer wants disproportionately high value for their time and money – in that order: time and money. And 2026 has been a year of growth across content consumption. The overall pie has increased, but the way it is sliced, and where growth and decline are happening, is constantly shifting.
This year has seen a major return to cinemas. The habit that COVID disrupted, but which began rebuilding gradually from 2022 and 2023, has demonstrated that people are willing to go to theatres. Films that succeed seem to have no ceiling. We are seeing bigger blockbusters at the level of individual films than ever before.
At the same time, we are seeing rejection at an unprecedented level. There is no ceiling to how well a film can perform, but there is also no floor to how badly it can do. Audiences are exercising their choices more decisively.
DEADLINE: So how do you meet the challenge?
Malhotra: To align with it, you have to keep sight of where the goalposts will be when your film or series is ready to be consumed. Novelty is also being rewarded, and that is something Abundantia has factored in from the beginning. It is becoming a significant moat for us. New worlds, new characters, new forms and disruptive genres are becoming the need of the hour.
The market is becoming more challenging, but that does not necessarily mean there is a recession. The kind and volume of content being sought are being defined more sharply. Everyone is focusing more on engagement, return on investment and a forward-looking perspective, rather than simply buying something off the shelf to meet demand for the following weekend.
That mindset is gone. This is a healthy correction and a timely rationalisation. It will improve the overall health of the business and allow quality players—and customer-focused platforms, streamers, networks and cinemas – to prosper.
results.summary:
India’s Abundantia Entertainment is transitioning its internal AI division, AiOn, into a standalone native studio to develop hybrid content and harness ideas from non-traditional creative sources.

### Key Points
- Abundantia Entertainment founder Vikram Malhotra announced that AiOn will launch as a fully independent AI studio by 2027.
- The studio will produce both fully generated and hybrid content, managing the entire production ecosystem.
- AiOn is currently collaborating with AI video technology company InVideo on a slate of five upcoming films.
- The initiative follows a significant increase in story pitches from creators outside the traditional filmmaking industry.
- Current projects in development include *Chiranjeevi Hanuman* and *Jai Santoshi Mata: Sukh Sampatti Daata*.

### Why it Matters
This move signals a shift toward integrating AI as a core production pillar rather than a mere cost-saving tool in the Indian entertainment market. By institutionalizing AI-driven workflows, Abundantia aims to mitigate financial risk and tap into a new generation of creators who are leveraging technology to bypass conventional industry gatekeepers.

results.title: As Trump touts his economic record, Vance acknowledges Americans’ concerns
results.author: Hannah Demissie
results.content:
It depends on who you ask: Trump and Vance offer slightly different takes on the economy
As Trump touts his economic record, Vance acknowledges Americans’ concerns.
As the midterms present a referendum on his second term, President Donald Trump continues to boast about his handling of the economy despite low approval ratings saying Americans aren't feeling it.
But while Trump has tried to paint a rosy picture of the economy, Vice President JD Vance has been driving home a different message on the campaign trail -- appearing more sympathetic to the economic squeeze frustrated voters are facing. Vance has also said the administration has made progress on that front, but urged voters to give them more time.
At several campaign rallies, Vance has urged patience, telling voters that "Rome wasn't built in a day."
According to a late September AP-NORC poll, 82% of adults disapprove of Trump's handling of the cost of living and only 17% approve.
Despite polls consistently showing that many Americans are not pleased with the effect of Trump's economic policies, the president continues to praise his record.
On his way to a campaign event in Texas last week, Trump told reporters he gave himself an "A+" across the board and discounted the economic pain from the war with Iran as a tradeoff with preventing that country from building a nuclear weapon.
And Trump said he's had to campaign on his economic agenda and its results because other Republicans are not "selling" it enough.
Vance has taken a different tone than his boss, expressing sympathy for Americans' economic frustrations while touting the Trump administration's wins and progress, often encouraging voters to support Republicans in November so the work can continue.
"Everything was not going to be fixed in 18 months. But you can't ignore people's concerns," Vance said during an interview with Real America's Voice last week.
Asked for his message to voters last month at the All-In Summit, a gathering of business, tech and investment leaders, Vance urged them to give Republicans "another chance." 
"There's a lot of good that's been done, but there's a lot of work left to do. Don't give power to the people who cause the problems that we're fixing. Give us another chance -- or give us another couple of years to continue to work on the amazing things that we've been doing for the past two years," Vance said then.
Trump has previously said that it was his own party doing an "extremely poor job" of selling his agenda and that's why he's touting his record.
"There are by a lot more Americans working today than at any time in the history of our country ... .but nobody knows it. That's why I'm doing it myself," Trump said in late September. "I'm going out because nobody's selling it. I'm doing, we're doing an extremely poor job of promotion and an extremely great job of running the country. So, I think you're probably better off with that. But we'll get the word out. It should not be hard."
But even though Trump has been touting job growth, the September jobs report showed only 29,000 jobs added, far below expectations. The report also reflected that wages are not keeping up with inflation.
When asked about the difference in economic messaging between Trump and Vance, the White House said that the two men are sharing the same message.
"President Trump and Vice President Vance are sharing the same message with the American people: if Republicans hold Congress and keep delivering on President Trump's agenda, American families will have more money in their pockets, secure borders, and safer streets."
Vance is viewed as a top Republican candidate for the White House in 2028. Asked by NBC News last week if Republicans not performing well in midterms would factor into his decision on whether to run for president, Vance said he would consider it.
"You make these decisions by collecting as much information and trying to make a wise decision. And, yeah, I mean, regardless of what happens over the next 35 days, there will be new information, new things you have to make a decision over."
results.summary:
President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance are employing distinct messaging strategies regarding the economy as they campaign for Republican candidates ahead of the upcoming midterm elections.

### Key Points
- President Trump maintains an "A+" rating for his economic record, citing job growth despite a September report showing only 29,000 jobs added.
- Vice President Vance acknowledges voter frustration with the cost of living, urging patience and asking for more time to implement the administration's agenda.
- An AP-NORC poll from late September indicates that 82% of adults disapprove of Trump’s handling of the cost of living.
- Trump attributes his need to personally promote his economic achievements to a perceived failure by other Republicans to effectively sell his policies.
- Vance, considered a potential 2028 presidential candidate, has stated he will evaluate his future political plans based on new information following the midterms.

### Why it Matters
The divergence in messaging highlights a strategic tension within the Republican Party as it attempts to address widespread voter dissatisfaction with inflation and economic conditions. How these differing approaches resonate with the electorate could influence midterm outcomes and shape the internal political landscape for the 2028 presidential cycle.

results.title: Anduril wants to be the 'next great American icon.' Its CMO has 3 rules for every campaign.
results.author: Polly Thompson
results.content:
Defense contractors are built to win procurement battles, not advertising awards.
The industry favors trade shows and low public profiles over flashy marketing campaigns, but defense tech startup Anduril is doing things differently. The startup "isn't hiding in the shadows," its marketing chief told Business Insider.
Anduril, founded by Palmer Luckey and four others in 2017, is on a mission to disrupt and accelerate America's weapons manufacturing with its sleek, easily manufactured autonomous weapons.
"The founders are creating the type of environment where they expect the same boldness from our marketing and creative work as they do from how we approach contracts or how we think about product development," Jeff Miller, Anduril's CMO, said in an interview.
He wants the brand to become the "next great American icon."
Every campaign is underpinned by three criteria, Miller said:
- Is it simple?
- Is it surprising?
- Is it elegant in its form?
The marketing must be connected to the company's soul and executed with "clear craft."
Its current program, the AI Grand Prix, is a perfect example of that strategy — bringing recruitment and marketing together on a global scale, with a bit of added fun.
The AI Grand Prix
Instead of simply posting an engineering job listing, the company is hosting an "AI Grand Prix" — a monthslong autonomous-drone racing competition with a $500,000 prize and a potential job at the $61 billion defense-tech company.
3,282 teams from around the world registered, including teams from South Korea, the Netherlands, Kazakhstan, and China, said Miller.
Miller spoke to Business Insider on the day of the final qualifying round for the AI Grand Prix in September. Fifteen teams remained at the start of the day; only 10 would advance to compete in the final this December at Anduril's newly built 5 million-square-foot factory in Ohio.
To make it to the final, they had to race the same make of autonomous drones through a series of gates in a timed trial. The only variable is the software: teams cannot modify the hardware or take control once their lap begins.
Using the Grand Prix to fill one position sounds like a drawn-out recruitment process, but Miller said it was effective and had an "extremely high hit rate" in terms of the talent concentration.
The company is seeing wannabe employees' skills demonstrated in real time, he added. Anduril also timed the event to align with campus recruitment cycles, meaning that whether or not students are competing, they're brought into the Anduril world.
More of Anduril
Anduril is growing fast and hiring thousands of engineers and manufacturing technicians over the next two years, said Miller.
In another recent recruiting push, Anduril ran a reverse-psychology campaign under the slogan "Don't work at Anduril." The accompanying video ad mocked nap pods, distant leadership, and the supposed lack of mission synonymous with modern tech jobs.
But it goes further than recruitment. An undertaking like the drone race provides a "huge halo" effect for the overall brand, said Miller.
"Campaigns like this or 'Don't work at Anduril' — it has such a clear way of defining who Anduril is, bringing broader awareness to that."
Inside Anduril's marketing team
Anduril does most of its marketing in-house with a team of roughly 12, who work closely with the startup's design team.
Anduril's leadership team understands the value of brand marketing and meets with Miller every week, he said.
They recognize that having a broad audience understand the mission has long term-value, not only in recruiting top talent, but in building a "great, durable brand that is trusted by and understood by the broader audience."
The idea for the AI Grand Prix originated with Luckey. He stopped Miller in the hall at work one day and said, "Jeff, I want to create the world's pre-eminent drone race."
"Okay, tell me more," Miller recalled saying in response.
Miller's career before Anduril included stints at PepsiCo, Snap, and the autonomous-car company Cruise. Moving from consumer products to defense was a challenge, he said.
That included understanding what could be said publicly, learning the technical side of Anduril's work, and adapting to faster timelines. In previous jobs, Miller said he's had a clear line of sight to the road map months ahead of a campaign, or at least weeks out. At Anduril, things will change by the day.
Figuring out how to approach storytelling for defense contractors, US government departments, and allied nations, as well as investors and potential talent, was another challenge. Miller spoke to Business Insider two weeks before Anduril announced plans to build a $6.6 billion shipyard in tandem with the US Navy.
"It's really important for us to make sure that it's not insular and just talking about Anduril, but that it's always done through the customer lens, the war fighter lens, and that requires us taking that extra step to make sure that we have their point of view factored in," he said.
While they "have so much respect" for the traditional defense companies, Miller said transparency is important to Anduril. US taxpayers have a vested interest in where their dollars are going, he said. "We're being clear about why we're doing this."
results.summary:
Defense tech startup Anduril is disrupting traditional defense industry marketing by using bold, consumer-facing campaigns and global competitions to recruit top engineering talent and build brand awareness.

### Key Points
- Founded in 2017 by Palmer Luckey, Anduril is currently valued at $61 billion.
- The company is hosting an "AI Grand Prix" drone racing competition, attracting 3,282 global teams to compete for a $500,000 prize and potential employment.
- The final round of the drone competition will take place this December at Anduril’s new 5 million-square-foot manufacturing facility in Ohio.
- Anduril plans to hire thousands of engineers and manufacturing technicians over the next two years to support its rapid growth.
- The company recently announced plans to construct a $6.6 billion shipyard in partnership with the U.S. Navy.

### Why it Matters

results.title: US stock market hits all-time high as investors bet big on AI
results.author: John Power
results.content:
The United States stock market has hit an all-time high as excitement around artificial intelligence continues to fuel a buying frenzy on Wall Street.
The S&P 500, the benchmark stock index, closed 0.58 percent higher on Tuesday, topping the previous peak reached in mid-August.
The Nasdaq Composite, which is more heavily weighted towards tech stocks, also hit a record high, finishing up 0.45 percent.
Tech stocks were among the top performers, with each of the “Magnificent Seven” apart from Meta closing higher.
Amazon led the pack with a 1.95 percent gain, followed by Microsoft and Tesla, which rose 0.78 percent and 0.51 percent, respectively.
Apple and Alphabet both rose 0.22 percent, while Nvidia gained 0.14 percent.
Meta, which has risen more than 20 percent since the launch last month of its new AI assistant, Muse, fell 0.41 percent.
Other big movers in tech included Marvell Technology, which rose 5.81 percent, and Cisco, which gained 4.54 percent.
Technology, AI
Keith Lerner, chief investment officer and chief market strategist at Truist Advisory Services in Atlanta, Georgia, said the market rally should be seen as a “technology and AI surge”.
“Every bull market has a dominant theme, and technology and AI remain this market’s dominant theme,” Lerner told Al Jazeera.
“Technology and communication services were the only two S&P 500 sectors to rise last month, while the other nine declined.”
Wall Street has shrugged off a host of challenges facing the US economy amid hyperscalers’ multibillion-dollar investments in AI.
Despite the energy crunch caused by the US-Israel war on Iran and a sell-off of US government bonds partly driven by ballooning government debt, the market is well on track to record its fourth consecutive year of double-digit returns.
The S&P 500 has risen 14 percent so far in 2026, while the Nasdaq Composite is up 18.78 percent.
“Investors remain bullish on the prospects for AI,” Lochlan Halloway, a senior equity strategist at Morningstar Australia, told Al Jazeera.
“They are betting that the money pouring into data centres will earn a good return, and so far, that belief has outweighed rising interest rates, more expensive oil and a 10-year bond yield above 5 percent,” Halloway said.
“We are positive on AI too,” Halloway added. “But the range of outcomes is wide, and the market is concentrated in a handful of companies, so the outlook for US shares, and by extension global shares, relies on the AI story continuing to deliver.”
Lerner at Truist Advisory said the market rally had the potential to continue through the end of 2026 given historical trends and expectations for strong corporate earnings.
“We do not expect a straight line higher for markets,” Lerner said.
“Still, the fourth quarter of [US] midterm-election years has produced an average gain of 7 percent and has been positive 84 percent of the time since 1950.”
Lerner said that rising interest rates posed the biggest risk to the upward trend.
“Still, on balance, the weight of the evidence suggests this bull market still has more upside potential,” he said.
Despite the rally on Wall Street, Asian stock markets fell on Wednesday, with key indexes in Japan, South Korea, and Hong Kong racking up losses.
The Kospi in Seoul led the sell-off, falling 1.98 percent, while Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 dropped 0.92 percent.
In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index was down 0.57 percent shortly before the market’s close.
Oil prices, which have been elevated since the start of the war on Iran, rose on Wednesday as traders weighed the fallout of fighting in Yemen between forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognised government and the Iran-aligned Houthis.
Brent crude futures for December delivery stood at $101.16 a barrel as of 07:30 GMT, up 0.58 percent.
results.summary:
The United States stock market reached record highs on Tuesday as sustained investor enthusiasm for artificial intelligence drove significant gains across the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite indexes.

### Key Points
- The S&P 500 rose 0.58 percent to reach a new all-time high, while the Nasdaq Composite climbed 0.45 percent.
- Amazon led the "Magnificent Seven" tech stocks with a 1.95 percent gain, followed by Microsoft and Tesla.
- Marvell Technology and Cisco saw significant growth, rising 5.81 percent and 4.54 percent, respectively.
- The S&P 500 has recorded a 14 percent increase so far in 2026, with the Nasdaq up 18.78 percent.
- Market analysts attribute the rally to massive capital investment in AI data centers despite rising interest rates and geopolitical tensions.

### Why it Matters
The current market rally highlights a heavy reliance on the artificial intelligence sector to drive global equity performance. While investors remain optimistic about long-term returns, the concentration of growth in a few tech companies creates significant vulnerability if the AI sector fails to meet high earnings expectations.

results.title: The best October Prime Day deals from Apple, Sony, Google, and more
results.author: Cameron Faulkner
results.content:
Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days event will end at 3AM ET on Thursday, October 8th. Many of the best deals are still happening, and it’s possible that more than a few of them will stick around even after the sale is over.
It’s your last chance to save on our favorite October Prime Day deals
Time is nearly up on Prime Big Deal Days, but some deals may stick around.
Our team cross-referenced shopping sites with our own reviews and buying guides, and found around 100 deals on some of the Verge staff’s favorite gadgets. Prime subscribers will get access to the most deals, though many of them are price-matched at retailers like Best Buy, Walmart, and Target.
We’ve got you if you’d rather check out some of the best deals under $25, or if you want just the best Apple deals. There are some great robot vacuum/mop deals, too.
Costco members can get in on the biggest price drop yet on the Legion Go 2, one of the most powerful gaming handhelds around.
The latest iteration of Apple’s Watch lineup is already discounted at Amazon.
The iPhone Air is Apple’s thinnest iPhone yet at 5.6mm, featuring a 6.5-inch ProMotion display, a 48MP fusion camera, and an 18MP front camera with Center Stage support. But its single rear camera and “meh” battery life mean it’s not for everyone.
The iPhone 16E is the spiritual successor to the iPhone SE, bringing flagship-level performance for less than the standard 16. We really wish it included MagSafe for $599, but those upgrading from older iPhones will probably be satisfied with what’s included.
While it won’t charge your Switch 2 any faster than the cheaper Belkin option, the clever battery-meets-kickstand with a built-in display simply looks better.
Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.
Roku’s latest Ultra streamer has built-in ethernet, a rechargeable voice remote with backlit buttons, and AirPlay 2 support. You can also control it with Amazon Alexa through a compatible smart speaker. The Roku Channel app lets you stream over 400 free live TV stations, plus exclusive movies like Weird: The Al Yankovic Story.
Roku’s Streaming Stick Plus supports 4K playback and features a slim design, so it won’t block nearby ports. It plugs straight into your TV’s HDMI port and can be powered by your TV’s USB port, so you don’t need an additional plug. It also comes with Roku’s Voice Remote, giving you hands-free control.
The WiiM Mini makes it easy to wirelessly stream music from your phone, a streaming service, or other local storage to existing speakers you already have. It supports AirPlay 2 and a variety of streaming services.
The Sub 4, while not cheap, is the best sub for your Sonos setup. It can sit upright, or you can lay it down to fit under a couch or entertainment system.
Google’s biggest Pixel 11 Pro got a sizeable price cut, too, making it $300 cheaper than the base iPhone 18 Pro Max model.
Apple’s new iteration of its priciest, most powerful headphones deliver minor updates for first-gen owners. But those who are jumping in will especially appreciate their big, bold sound. Read our review.
Roku’s latest Pro 4K TV has a 120Hz refresh rate, four HDMI ports (two of which are 2.1), full-array local dimming for even brightness, and support for both Dolby Vision IQ and HDR 10 Plus for better color accuracy. It also works with Apple Home, Amazon Alexa, and Google Home, making it easy to integrate into most smart homes.
The Kindle Scribe Colorsoft is Amazon’s first note-taking e-reader with a color screen. It features an 11-inch display, a slimmer design, an improved interface, an updated stylus, and a new AI-powered search feature that can quickly summarize documents.
The third-gen Kindle Scribe 32GB is even bigger than its 10.2-inch predecessor; it offers an 11-inch display with 300ppi resolution and the same great battery life that Kindles are known for.
Amazon’s last-gen Kindle Colorsoft features a color E Ink screen, offering similar performance to the new 2026 model. It also offers eight weeks of battery life and a 7-inch display that’s great for comics and graphic novels. Read our review.
A new version of the Fit Pro wireless earbuds, which are upgraded with a redesigned wing tip that Beats says is 20 percent more flexible, a smaller case, and other advantages.
The latest Powerbeats Pro are a no-brainer for athletes. They pack fantastic sound and thumping bass, along with active noise cancellation, IPX4 water resistance, and heart rate monitoring. Read our review.
Powered by Apple’s new M5 chip, the latest MacBook Airs are more powerful than prior models and offer double the base storage (512GB). They also support faster wireless standards, specifically Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Read our review.
For a slightly bigger MacBook Air, the 15-inch version is the one to get. It offers similar performance, but its battery is larger, and it has more speakers.
Bose’s SoundLink Max improves on the smaller Flex with true stereo sound — and very powerful sound at that. It’s got a removable handle for easy transport, and there’s an aux input for playing audio when you want to listen at a higher quality than what Bluetooth can deliver. Read our review.
The second-gen SoundLink Flex builds on the original with more intuitive controls, including a new play / pause button. It also adds adjustable EQ and support for higher-quality audio via AAC and aptX, while retaining a rugged IP67-rated design and the ability to pair two speakers for stereo sound.
The case features an integrated power bank and a small pocket to stow an AirTag (or other similarly sized Bluetooth tracker).
A slick 2-in-1 charger that can charge your magnet-friendly iPhone or Pixel at a relatively speedy pace. Its extra charging pad supports AirPods, the Apple Watch, and other Qi-ready accessories.
An affordable color-accurate monitor that can easily connect to a MacBook or Windows machine that has USB-C video support. It’s a good price for a fully-featured 1440p monitor.
Slap a recent iPhone onto this charging pad and it’ll charge at fast 25W speeds. It can also charge AirPods, and includes a cord and wall adapter.
Xreal’s most affordable set of USB-C display glasses yet. They lack three degrees of freedom, but are otherwise an awesome value for gaming or watching movies with your own huge, private screen. Read our hands-on.
Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.
Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.
This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It will also work with the new Aliro standard and be compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking.
The G400 was the first wired-only video doorbell to work with Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video feature. It has solid specs for the price, and includes a chime to sound indoors.
The Restore 3 features more than 50 sleep sounds and 18 adjustable light colors, with access to hundreds more through the optional Hatch Plus subscription, which runs $4.99 per month or $49.99 per year.
LifeStraw’s basic filter removes unwanted bacteria and microplastics as you drink, giving you a safe way to hydrate no matter where you are.
A smart plug adds functionality to an existing gadget rather than replacing it. Once the plug is connected to your Wi-Fi network and a gadget, you can turn it on and off using an app. TP-Link’s Tapo smart plug supports Matter, so you can add it to whichever smart home platform you use.
A semi-affordable (subscription-free) outdoor security camera that supplies both a floodlight and a pan/tilt design so that you can easily track visitors.
If you’re itching to locally host photos, files, videos, and more instead of paying for cloud storage, this entry-level NAS from Ugreen is discounted. You’ll just need to pack it with NAS-ready HDDs.
While not the fastest wireless charger at this price, Anker’s unique, UFO-styled 3-in-1 charging puck unfolds with pads for a phone, AirPods, and an Apple Watch.
Anker’s powerful Nano international travel charger is great if you have a lot of USB-C gadgets to keep charged. While it lacks an AC plug, it supplies a screen that shows how much power you’re pushing to each port.
Anker’s latest single-port USB-C charger offers up to 45W of power, foldable prongs, and a front-facing “smart display” that lets you see the charge level, power flow, and other useful information at a glance.
These smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible.
Philips Hue bulbs can be pricey, which is why the company’s four-pack of Essential A19 bulbs are a great buy. They’re cheaper, costing less now during Prime Day than usual. They have adjustable colors, brightness, and can be controlled with Bluetooth or with a Hue Bridge (sold separately).
Bissell’s Little Green is handy, but doesn’t cut it for big jobs. If you have pets and a lot of carpet to clean, this is one of the most powerful upright carpet cleaners in its price range.
It’s a Lightwall. What more do you need to know? Fine, it’s a curtain of lights that’s 8.5 feet wide and 6.2 feet tall with 1,536 LEDs. You can program them to show anything you want.
The outdoor lamp post light boasts full support for Google Assistant, Alexa, and Matter, so you can easily incorporate the lights into your smart home setup.
The color-changing Govee Table Lamp 2 is an especially great pick for grads looking to make a new space feel like home. With adjustable warmth and brightness, plus lights that sync to music, it’s easy to set the mood for relaxing, focusing, or partying. It can also be controlled with voice assistants or a simple tap for added convenience.
This 10,000mAh power bank is one of the best ones available at this price. It has a built-in USB-C cable, and it’s MagSafe-ready, supporting up to 25W wireless charging speed for recent iPhones. Read our coverage.
A new third-person adventure game made by several developers responsible for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Dawnwalker is similar in terms of its branching storyline and great side quests, but unique with how vampirism affects gameplay.
A 2800-lumen light that can illuminate your desk area for video meetings, close work, and other uses. It includes a desk clamp to make it easy to fix to your working surface.
One of the most well-rounded Android gaming handhelds you can buy is the Retroid Pocket 5. It has a gorgeous 5.5-inch OLED screen, a PS Vita-like design, and enough power to play games up to the PS2 era thanks to its Snapdragon 865 processor.
Nothing’s first pair of over-ear headphones feature a retro transparent design and high-end features like active noise cancellation, spatial audio with head tracking, and plush ear pads. They also feature a paddle button that allows you to control music playback. Read our review.
The Xeneon Edge is a multipurpose touchscreen for your PC that gives you easy access to controls, various metrics, and widgets of your choosing through Corsair’s marketplace.
$1,000 doesn’t usually get you all that much in a laptop these days, but it does during October Prime Day. This model has a 14-inch OLED screen, 16GB RAM, a 1TB SSD, and a capable Intel Core Ultra 7 CPU.
A screen-free device for kids that plays songs or stories when you tap collectible Tonie figures on the top of it. It’s for entertainment, but can double as an alarm.
An incredible value if you want one of the most comfortable right-handed wireless mice currently available. This price applies to the black or white versions.
A teleprompter is a luxury. They help you make it look effortless to look at your camera as you read from a script or a chat log. Elgato’s option includes a small screen and a mirror, the latter of which allows you to see what you need to look at without breaking eye contact with viewers.
The MK.2 version of the standard Stream Deck comes with 15 programmable buttons, a swappable faceplate, and a detachable stand.
This wall adapter can deliver up to 140W when you’re using just one of its four ports. But even with to four gadgets, it can divvy up 140W so each gets a good amount of power.
If you want to bring your home theater to the next level, the Samsung Q990F is the answer. The Q990 series has been at the top of best lists for years, and for good reason. It delivers an excellent Atmos experience with clear dialogue and booming bass to fully immerse you in whatever you’re watching.
The hourglass-shaped Sonos Era 300 is designed from the ground up for spatial audio and Dolby Atmos. It supports the same Bluetooth and line-in features as the Era 100.
Those in need of a capable, compact, and somewhat affordable Windows laptop should consider the Aspire Lite 14. It’s an ARM-based machine with 16GB of speedy RAM, half a terabyte of storage, and a slick design.
The OpenRun Pro 2 are Shokz’s best bone conduction headphones yet, with better sound and more bass than their predecessor. Our reviewer Victoria Song praised their cozy fit as well as their USB-C charging (goodbye, proprietary charger!). Read our review.
This XCOM-inspired twist of a Star Wars tactics game is as good as it sounds. Snag the game on its first-ever discount.
A smart speaker with a HomePod-like design that’s compatible with many more services. It even has a cool, little screen on the front.
The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.
A powerful tablet that can turn into a laptop when you purchase the keyboard+trackpad accessory. This model features an OLED screen, the Snapdragon X2 Elite, 16GB RAM and a 512GB SSD. Read our coverage.
Launched in late July, the Sleepbuds 2 have a small design that’s ideal for side sleepers. They can supply audio with 14 hours of battery life, and even a private alarm that’ll wake you (and not others in bed).
Fujifilm’s stylish Instax Mini Evo is the best instant camera overall. With it, you can choose which photos to print, while also boasting good image quality.
While a relatively minor upgrade over the C5 if you’re getting a 65-inch or smaller screen, the 77- and 83-inch C6 utilize an improved Tandem OLED screen with incredible brightness.
The latest Surface Pro is speedy and elegant, with a 13-inch OLED touchscreen and the Snapdragon X2 Elite processor. It doesn’t include a keyboard, though.
The latest iteration of Apple’s iPad Air features an M4 processor and better connectivity under the hood, resulting in great performance whether you’re gaming or doing AI-related tasks. Read our review.
The Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 is a fun gift for students starting a new chapter. It prints credit card-sized photos in seconds, and the new self-timer makes it easier to snap group photos with friends.
Apple’s entry-level iPad is an excellent tablet for casual use, even if it is getting a little long in the tooth. Its high-res screen is great for watching video, and its A16 processor is still fast enough to handle light games and productivity apps. Read our review.
Sony made subtle improvements to every facet of the WH-1000XM6, from sound quality to ANC performance, while wisely bringing back the foldable, travel-friendly design last seen on the XM4.
The first Sony OLED with four HDMI 2.1 ports. It competes with the LG C6 in terms of brightness and specs, and this is its first big price drop.
Pokémon Legends: Z-A is the first game in the main series with a real-time battling system instead of the traditional turn-based formula. You’re still catching pokémon, leveling up, trading, and battling in the game’s Paris-inspired setting, but the more action-oriented battles and smooth performance (on the Nintendo Switch 2) are very welcome.
Apple’s AirPods 4 are last-gen wireless earbuds, but they’re still great. The hard, plastic buds feature improved audio over the third-gen model, along with deep iOS integration and spatial audio with head tracking. Read our review.
The 27GX704A-B is a glossy OLED monitor with a 240Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, HDMI 2.1 ports, a DisplayPort input, and other nice-to-have features.
This ultrawide (21:9) QHD OLED gaming monitor has a 280Hz refresh rate, a fast response time, and a slick design. It’s tough to get more OLED for your money than with this model when it’s discounted.
The discounted Ninja Slushi produces up to 88 ounces of smoothies without using any ice. It can keep drinks cold for up to 12 hours, with five temperature presets for dialing in your experience.
The G309 is an inexpensive, dual-mode wireless gaming mouse that punches well above its weight. It’s equipped with the same Hero 25K sensor and hybrid optomechanical switches found on pricier models, along with up to 600 hours of runtime over Bluetooth. It’s also the cheapest Powerplay mouse you can get, if you want to skip the whole charging thing altogether.
Samsung’s Galaxy 8 smartwatch features a squircle design, Gemini, and some health features like an Antioxidant Index and Running Coach.

results.title: I ditched my cloud password manager for KeePassXC, and I feel more secure than ever
results.author: Oluwaseun Bamisile
results.content:
For a long time, I've used LastPass, a cloud-based password manager. I even paid the $3-per-month subscription fee for the extra perks, and I stuck with it even after its infamous 2022 security breach. But then, LastPass had another security incident this year, and although it wasn't as damaging as the 2022 incident, it became an eye-opener for me.
I started thinking about how much control I was actually giving a company over one of the most sensitive collections of information I have. So, I decided to go local.
KeePassXC gives me total control over my password database
My passwords aren't sitting on someone else's servers
Cloud password managers like LastPass handle everything for you and store passwords in the cloud. KeePassXC, on the other hand, says, “take these password management tools and knock yourself out.” And on top of that, everything stays with you.
I didn’t even have to create an account or anything. I just create a password database stored in a .kdbx file on my device. KeePassXC also gives me plenty of options for how I build and use my password database. For example, I can add custom fields to entries when the default fields aren't enough and even choose the encryption method I want. I can structure my database however I want instead of being locked into whatever fields a cloud password manager gives me.
Plugins and extensions also add functionality, plus portable installation options if I want to run KeePassXC without installing it the traditional way. And if I'm willing to get a little more technical, I can even use scripts and integrations for things like working with SSH agents and other tools in my workflow.
Although it's desktop-only, I can still sync my passwords across devices
Moving my vault between devices takes more effort, but I have more control over how it happens
When I first switched to a local password manager, one of the biggest things I had to get used to was the lack of built-in synchronization. LastPass made this easy since I could sign into my account on another device and my passwords were already there.
While KeePassXC is primarily a desktop application, the .kdbx file is portable and can be accessed on other devices. So, with the help of Syncthing, I was able to synchronize my KeePassXC database across multiple devices.
KeePassXC also works with compatible mobile apps. On Android, you have KeePassDX and KeePass2Android, while iPhone and iPad users get Strongbox or KeePassium. These apps allow you to open, edit, and sync your .kdbx password databases on smartphones and tablets
With great control comes great responsibility
I have to take backups and encryption seriously
Having complete control over my password database also means I can't blame anyone else if I mess something up. I’m basically in charge of everything, so keeping my database safe is totally up to me. First, I needed a strong master password. I use something long, at least 15 characters, rather than relying on a short password with a few numbers and symbols thrown in.
I also need to think about backups. The 3-2-1 backup strategy works for me: three copies of my important data, stored on two different types of media, with one copy kept somewhere else. I also recommend storing a secondary physical key file on a secure USB drive rather than relying solely on your master password.
KeePassXC also gives me modern encryption options, including AES-256 and ChaCha20. Meanwhile, its key derivation functions, such as Argon2 and PBKDF2, make brute-force attacks harder.
Sometimes control is better than convenience
Switching from a cloud password manager like LastPass to KeePassXC wasn't all that easy. I had to get used to managing my own database, figuring out synchronization, and taking responsibility for my backups. But I also gained something I didn't realize I was missing: control.
I own the actual password database; I decide where it lives, how it's backed up, which devices can access it, and how I want to customize the way it works. There’s no denying cloud password managers are the more convenient option, but I prefer knowing that my password vault isn't dependent on a company's servers.
results.summary:
Users are increasingly migrating from cloud-based password managers like LastPass to local, open-source alternatives like KeePassXC to gain greater control over their sensitive data and security protocols.

### Key Points
- KeePassXC allows users to store password databases locally in a .kdbx file, eliminating reliance on third-party cloud servers.
- The software supports advanced encryption standards, including AES-256 and ChaCha20, alongside key derivation functions like Argon2.
- Users can synchronize local databases across devices using third-party tools like Syncthing or compatible mobile apps such as Strongbox and KeePassDX.
- Transitioning to a local manager requires users to manage their own backups, often utilizing the 3-2-1 strategy to prevent data loss.
- KeePassXC offers high customizability, including support for custom entry fields, plugins, and portable installation options for advanced workflows.

### Why it Matters
Shifting to local password management reflects a growing trend of users prioritizing data sovereignty over the convenience of cloud-based services following high-profile security breaches. While this approach demands more technical responsibility, it mitigates the risk of centralized server attacks and ensures users maintain full ownership of their digital credentials.

results.title: Attackers Hide AI Prompt Injections Inside Phishing Emails
results.author: Alessandro  Mascellino
results.content:
Phishing emails have been found carrying hidden instructions for AI assistants alongside conventional lures for the human recipient, meaning that a single message targets both the user and the system that summarizes their inbox.
In research published on October 7, Barracuda said it analyzed a campaign that combined traditional social engineering, such as password-protected attachments, with prompt injection concealed in the same message. It did not say how widespread the campaign was.
The sample looked like ordinary internal correspondence. Its "From" and "To" addresses matched the same mailbox, it carried a trusted spam confidence score and it came from a public-sector domain, which helped it pass reputation-based filtering.
One Email, Two Targets
For the human, the email carried a password-protected attachment with the password supplied in the message body, a tactic Barracuda said creates a blind spot for traditional email security controls. Opening it would lead to credential theft or malware delivery.
If the recipient overlooked the message, the hidden prompt injection could make their AI assistant present it as legitimate or urgent in its summary, pushing them to open the email and click the link.
Barracuda said four techniques featured frequently in hiding such instructions: HTML comments, invisible text styled with CSS, Base64-encoded data and zero-width characters.
Injected instructions could also tell an assistant to ignore its previous directions and request a wire transfer, leak data or surface a fake urgent action.
Wider Targets Call For Layered Defenses
Among real-world examples, Barracuda described a hidden block in an invoice email that told the summarizing AI to add a fake priority action changing vendor payment details, nudging an employee toward wiring money to the attacker.
It also described hidden text in a resume telling an AI screening tool to rate the candidate 10 out of 10, a fake maintenance-mode request to make a support bot reveal its configuration and poisoned web documentation that could make a coding assistant insert a credential-exfiltration line into authentication code.
Barracuda said no single control would stop every variation. It recommended stripping hidden elements and invisible characters before content reaches AI systems, detecting instruction-override language, AI sandboxing, output validation and human approval for payments and vendor changes. It also advised monitoring for repeated injection attempts.
It said external content should always be treated as data, kept separate from instructions.
results.summary:
Cybersecurity researchers at Barracuda have identified a new phishing tactic that uses hidden prompt injections to manipulate AI email assistants while simultaneously targeting human users with traditional malware.

### Key Points
- Barracuda researchers discovered phishing emails containing hidden instructions designed to deceive AI summarization tools alongside conventional social engineering lures.
- Attackers use techniques like HTML comments, invisible CSS-styled text, Base64 encoding, and zero-width characters to conceal malicious prompts from human readers.
- Injected instructions can force AI assistants to prioritize fake invoices, alter vendor payment details, or misrepresent the urgency of malicious emails.
- The campaign successfully bypassed reputation-based filters by utilizing trusted public-sector domains and matching sender and recipient addresses.
- Recommended defenses include stripping hidden content before AI processing, implementing output validation, and requiring human approval for sensitive financial transactions.

### Why it Matters
This dual-threat approach exploits the growing reliance on AI assistants to summarize and prioritize daily communications, creating a new vector for credential theft and financial fraud. Organizations must now implement layered security strategies that treat external content as untrusted data to prevent AI systems from being weaponized against their users.

results.title: S&P 500 Hits Record High as Tech Gains Mask Broad Market Weakness
results.author: Chase Codewell
results.content:
The index rose 0.6% to close at 7,819.04, its first record since August, according to Barron's [1]. The tech-heavy Nasdaq composite also reached a record, rising 0.45%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped from its own record high [2]. The New York Times reported the S&P 500's gain Tuesday took its advance this year to more than 14% [3].
The rally was concentrated in a handful of megacap technology companies. Nvidia rose 4.5% over the past week to an all-time high, and Meta Platforms gained 24% since Aug. 13, according to market data. Most other S&P 500 stocks declined, including healthcare firms, banks and consumer staple companies, while small-cap stocks and the Dow industrials also fell, the data showed. Fewer than half of the stocks in the S&P 500 closed above their 200-day moving average on Tuesday, a figure that has steadily declined since August.
Market breadth has narrowed in recent weeks, with the equal-weighted version of the S&P 500 and the Russell 2000 small-cap index trailing the capitalization-weighted S&P 500 over the past month, according to market data. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also trailed the S&P 500 over the same period.
Analysts said the market's narrow breadth could pose a risk to investors because returns are increasingly reliant on a small group of stocks that can swing on concerns ranging from AI spending to declining free cash flow. The Wall Street Journal reported that most U.S. stocks are down even as the market's AI engine is "firing on all cylinders" [4].
Other analysts noted the market has been reliant on technology's success for several years, with ultimately good results. MarketWatch described the megacap technology group as having returned to being "the workhorse of the U.S. equity market" [5]. Chris Martenson of Peak Prosperity wrote that markets driven by "a cycle of excitement and hype" can lead to "unsustainable behaviors" [6].
A United States Military Academy professor said the productivity promises behind artificial intelligence are reshaping how firms and investors assess value, adding that the technology has become a defining factor in equity markets.
Many investors now view AI-focused technology companies as insulated from the effects of higher interest rates, analysts said. Big technology companies, including Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta, have traditionally been cash-rich and relatively debt-free, though many are now raising tens of billions of dollars to finance the AI build-out, according to company disclosures and analysts.
The combined market capitalization of the Magnificent Seven closed at a record high on Tuesday of roughly $25 trillion, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The tech-stock performance helped indexes rise amid a global bond selloff that drove Treasury yields to multi-decade highs. The 10-year Treasury yield eased 0.040 percentage points to settle at 5.270%, according to market data.
Analysts said the so-called narrow breadth could pose a risk, with equity market returns solely reliant on a small group of stocks that can swing on external threats such as Chinese AI models or superintelligence doomsday scenarios. The National News Desk reported that Wall Street's securities industry posted record first-half profits of $45.9 billion, according to a report released by New York State Comptroller Thomas DiNapoli on Oct. 6, a 51% year-over-year increase [7].
The S&P 500's advance has been powered by a narrow group of stocks tied to the artificial-intelligence trade. Barron's reported the benchmark index climbed 0.6% to close at a fresh record of 7,819.04, its first high since August [1].
MarketWatch reported the S&P 500 is back in record territory as the "Magnificent Seven" megacap tech stocks "ride to the rescue" [5]. CNBC reported the index returned to an intraday record Tuesday as "tech gains, easing oil prices and Treasury yields helped stocks overcome months of market shocks" [8].
The Guardian reported that at the market's close, the S&P 500 was up 0.58%, topping 7,800 for the first time in its history, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq index rose 0.45% and the Dow was slightly down from its record high [2]. The Financial Post reported that "a gauge of megacaps rose 1.4 per cent" as the S&P 500 approached a record, and that "Treasury 10-year yields hit the highest since 2002" [9].
Analysts said eye-watering earnings forecasts for AI-linked companies are expected to keep propelling technology names forward, even with higher rates and a cooling economy bearing down on the rest of the market. FactSet's bottom-up analyst target for the S&P 500 sits at 9,261, according to reporting by Lance Roberts [10].
Whether the rally broadens or remains concentrated depends on future earnings reports and Federal Reserve rate decisions, according to analysts. The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% in September, its first hike since 2023, according to reporting by Lance Roberts [11].
Market participants continue to monitor Treasury yields and breadth indicators, according to market data. Chris Martenson of Peak Prosperity wrote that while "markets may appear stable on the surface," there are "underlying economic pressures that could lead to" instability [6].
No consensus has emerged on whether narrow breadth signals a risk or reflects continued technology-led growth, analysts said.

Down but not out. Bitcoin's stair-step bullish trajectory is still intact
Bitcoin dipped to around $84,200 on Wednesday but stayed inside its recent range, keeping the broader bullish stair-step trajectory intact.
- Bitcoin fell to about $84,200 on Wednesday but remained within the $83,000-to-$87,000 range that has preserved its bullish stair-step pattern since July.
- Analysts said support near $83,000 is crucial, with a sustained break below $82,000 to $83,000 signaling that September’s breakout has failed.
- If that support gives way, Bitcoin could retreat toward $80,000 to $81,500, while holding it would suggest sellers cannot push the cryptocurrency back into its previous trading range.
Bitcoin  is on the back foot Wednesday. Its bigger bullish pattern is still holding.
The cryptocurrency fell to $84,200 early Wednesday, down over 2% from near $86,500 on Tuesday, according to CoinDesk data. But it's still trading inside the range it has held for the past two weeks, and that keeps a months-long bullish stair-step trajectory alive.
"The October 7 decline does not invalidate Bitcoin's stair-step rise," Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Indian crypto exchange Giottus, told CoinDesk.
Since July, bitcoin has climbed in a series of flat ranges, each higher than the last. On a chart, it looks like a set of stairs, which is why it's known as a stair-step pattern. As seen in the feature image, the sharp rallies are the climb from one stair to the next, and the weeks of sideways trading are the flat steps in between.
From mid-July to Aug. 18, it traded between roughly $62,000 and $67,000. Then it jumped 21% in three days.
The next step ran from late August to mid-September, between about $76,000 and $81,500. Another sudden jump followed, a 6.6% gain from Sept. 19 to Sept. 21.
Since then, bitcoin has held between about $83,000 and $87,000.
"After moving above $81,500, Bitcoin established a new range of roughly 83,000-87,000. If $83,000 holds, it would show that sellers cannot force the price back into its previous trading band," Subburaj said.
The key level to watch on the downside is near $83,000. A clear break below there would end the staircase, at least for now.
A sustained break below $82,000 to $83,000 would signal that the September breakout has failed and would bring $80,000 to $81,500 back into play, Subburaj said.
Alex Kuptsikevich, chief market analyst at FxPro, said support is somewhat higher, around $84,000, and that a break below it would open the door to $80,000.
As of this writing, BTC is trading near $84,300.
